Parse unfamiliar sentences into clauses and explain the function of major phrases and modifiers.
Generate at least five syntactically different sentences expressing the same logical proposition.
Use punctuation, coordination, subordination, and word order to control emphasis and relation rather than merely obey rules.
Diagnose ambiguity or unintended implication caused by grammatical structure and repair it without loss of nuance.
Define a word operationally enough to separate it from close alternatives, with positive examples and boundary cases.
Choose among near-synonyms by denotation, connotation, register, collocation, rhythm, and audience.
Recognize idiomatic versus merely grammatical phrasing and revise unnatural collocations.
Use dictionaries/corpora as evidence while resisting etymological fallacies and false precision.
Arrange sentences so given information leads readers toward new information with minimal processing confusion.
Build paragraphs with a discernible controlling movement rather than a pile of related statements.
Control pronoun/reference chains, transitions, parallel structure, and emphasis across multiple paragraphs.
Rewrite a confusing passage by changing order and information structure without simplifying the underlying idea.
Map an argument into claim, reasons, evidence, warrants, assumptions, and counterarguments.
Adapt the same proposition to hostile, neutral, expert, and general audiences without changing what counts as evidence.
Distinguish rhetorical effectiveness from logical or empirical support.
Concede, qualify, rebut, or revise in response to a serious counterargument rather than caricaturing opposition.
Translate an abstraction into concrete images and then recover the abstraction without distortion.
Generate multiple metaphors/analogies for one relation and identify where each mapping fails.
Distinguish symbol, metaphor, simile, metonymy, synecdoche, and literal description in actual passages.
Use figurative language to discover or compress thought rather than merely ornament prose.
Describe voice and tone through observable lexical, syntactic, rhythmic, and rhetorical features.
Rewrite one factual content block in at least five registers while keeping core facts invariant.
Construct reliable and unreliable personae and show how evidence creates the reader's trust or suspicion.
Use irony and distance without making the intended stance unrecoverable.
Separate event sequence from discourse order and explain how rearrangement changes suspense, causality, or sympathy.
Retell one event in first person, limited third, omniscient, and free indirect styles with controlled information access.
Move deliberately among scene, summary, pause, ellipsis, and description.
Design revelation and omission so the reader can infer more than is explicitly stated.
Identify speech acts and objectives beneath dialogue lines rather than treating dialogue as information transfer only.
Write a two-person scene where each speaker pursues a different objective and important information remains implicit.
Use interruption, silence, rhythm, gesture/stage information, and turn length as meaning-bearing devices.
Transform explanatory prose into playable dramatic action without losing necessary content.
Scan common accentual-syllabic lines and distinguish meter from actual performed rhythm.
Use rhyme, stress, alliteration, assonance, consonance, caesura, and repetition deliberately.
Explain how line breaks and enjambment alter syntax, pace, emphasis, and ambiguity.
Compose one idea in metrical verse, free verse, and rhythmic prose, then defend the formal tradeoffs.
Frame a genuine question and produce a thesis that is arguable, scoped, and answerable by available evidence.
Define, classify, compare, and explain complex material without hiding uncertainty.
Perform close textual analysis that connects quoted or described detail to an interpretive claim.
Write criticism that represents rival readings fairly and states what evidence would force revision.
Perform an unseen close reading at the levels of syntax, diction, image, sound, form, voice, and structure.
Distinguish genre convention from an author's specific deviation from convention.
Place major English-language forms and periods on a rough historical map without treating the map as a hierarchy of value.
Defend two competing interpretations of one passage and identify which details discriminate between them.
Identify a passage's generative style features without reducing style to surface adjectives.
Imitate structural mechanisms of a style using completely new subject matter and wording.
Paraphrase difficult prose into plain English, then restore complexity where simplification destroyed necessary distinctions.
Transform content across genre, length, voice, and register while explicitly tracking what must remain invariant.
Mark prose for breath, stress, pause, pace, and emphasis, then revise syntax to improve live intelligibility.
Deliver a short argument extemporaneously from an outline rather than reading sentences.
Use rhetorical repetition, parallelism, cadence, and timing without sounding accidental or inflated.
Diagnose the difference between a text that reads well silently and one that works when heard once.
Choose form, register, structure, syntax, diction, imagery, and rhythm from intention rather than habit.
Express one difficult proposition successfully as analytic explanation, persuasive argument, narrative, scene, lyric, speech, and concise summary.
Edit at conceptual, structural, paragraph, sentence, and word levels in the correct order.
Defend expressive choices under changed audience/medium constraints and revise immediately when the premise changes.

external_validation.provenance_status: Imported registry assertions; independent freeze and administration not verified in this audit

registry.principle: Use frozen unseen material where it can validly test intellectual or practical transfer, but do not pretend every life outcome has a clean hold-out. The Obelisk uses convergent evidence: external human acceptance criteria, professional standards, unseen transfer, adaptive-agency stress cases, real-world practice, and eventually longitudinal observation.

branches.contamination_control: corpus was recovered after the candidate graph existed; limitations documented in backtest data

branches.minimum_design: at least 60 cases spanning regions, eras, institution types and scales; selected by an independent curator after graph freeze
branches.scoring: independent reviewers classify route quality, missing foundational family, missing fact, mastery failure, and disagreement
branches.success: two heterogeneous rounds with no new load-bearing family

branches.minimum_design: unseen exposition, argument, interpretation, transformation, editing, speech, listening and audience-adaptation tasks; external texts not in the taught reading set
branches.scoring: expert/reader panel plus artifact rubric; include human-only and AI-assisted conditions
branches.success: no recurrent expressive capability outside the 14-module/56-outcome graph

branches.minimum_design: learn unfamiliar material or skill under declared conditions; delayed retention, calibration, transfer, teaching, and AI-offloading measures
branches.scoring: pre/post/delayed performance and blinded evaluation; not self-report alone
branches.success: failures trace to mastery/implementation rather than a missing learning capability family

branches.method: blinded design briefs and comparative critique
branches.minimum_design: unseen visual, data, spatial, object/interface and multimodal briefs plus blind ranking/critique sets from multiple traditions
branches.scoring: multiple expert/user reviewers; usability/reality measures where relevant; document inter-rater agreement
branches.success: no recurrent visual/spatial/interface/aesthetic-functional capability family outside the candidate graph

branches.method: existing proof-of-work plus future hidden technical perturbations
branches.minimum_design: unseen derivations, experiments, builds, failure injections and cross-domain technical cases
branches.scoring: objective tests where possible plus defense
branches.success: technical module granularity remains sufficient or decomposes only when repeated gaps demand it

registry.construct_warning: A hold-out corpus is evidence for a specific interpretation, not proof that a branch or the whole curriculum is universally valid.

all_souls_program.rationale: The All Souls Examination Fellowship is unusually valuable because it uses open-ended specialist/general papers plus viva to distinguish among exceptional candidates using published criteria for depth, argument, independence, sources, breadth, clarity, responsiveness and potential.
all_souls_program.current: 417 Philosophy + General prompts in canonical backtest data
all_souls_program.next: Backtest the frozen V0.4 graph against official Economics, English Literature, History, Law and Politics papers from available sittings; treat results as criterion-proxy evidence for HW/EX/general judgment, not complete life validation.

candidates.Core content: Algorithms; data structures; discrete models; computability; complexity; randomized/approximation ideas; cryptographic intuition.
candidates.Exit capability: Reconstruct algorithmic tradeoffs, reason about tractability, and detect when 'AI solved it' hides computational or verification costs.
candidates.Why current core may not cover it: Scientific computing is numerical; it does not substitute for general computer science.
candidates.Decision: ADMIT unless existing modules can absorb it without distortion.

candidates.Core content: Software architecture; testing; versioning; OS/processes; databases; networks; distributed consensus/failure; observability; privacy; secure development.
candidates.Exit capability: Design and audit a networked software service with explicit failure, security, data, and operational boundaries.
candidates.Why current core may not cover it: Advanced civilization and AI infrastructure are software/networked systems; this is currently implicit.
candidates.Decision: ADMIT unless TS23 is broadened enough without becoming unteachable.

candidates.Core content: Climate/energy balance; atmosphere/ocean circulation; water; soils; biogeochemical cycles; ecosystems; population/ecology; resource flows; environmental risk.
candidates.Exit capability: Trace coupled physical-biological-human constraints and identify hard planetary/transport/resource limits on interventions.
candidates.Why current core may not cover it: Physics + biology do not automatically produce usable Earth-system intuition.
candidates.Decision: KEEP AS CANDIDATE; backtest against climate, agriculture, water, biodiversity, mining, disaster cases.
